newsitem.title: CHILE: German fugitive sighting may have been a ploy - Chile.
newsitem.headline: German fugitive sighting may have been a ploy - Chile.

text.p: The surfacing in Argentina by a man calling himself Paul Schaefer, fugitive leader of a secretive German colony in southern Chile, may have been a diversionary ploy by the real Schaefer who is probably still in Chile, officials said on Sunday.

A man calling himself Schaefer checked into a hotel in the Argentine ski resort of Bariloche on Friday but apparently fled through a second-floor window when police, alerted by an anonymous phone call, knocked on his door, Argentine news reports said.
The police found only the man's pajamas in the room, the reports said.

The mysterious episode suggested that Schaefer, wanted on charges of sexually molesting boys at the German-speaking enclave of Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), had fled over the Andes into Argentina, but Chilean authorities said the incident may have been a red herring.

"This could be nothing more than a diversionary tactic," said deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco. The man who checked into the Bariloche hotel was taller and heavier than descriptions of the real Schaefer, Velasco said.
"The characteristics of the person in question don't match those of Paul Schaefer," Velasco said on local television.

He said authorities were not sure if Schaefer was still in Chile but that Colonia Dignidad, nestled among the Andean foothills near the town of Parral, "has thousands of hectares (acres) of forests and rivers, as well as tunnels and bunkers" where Schaefer could hide.

State television quoted police sources as saying Schaefer was probably still in Chile and that the Bariloche incident was likely a ploy to throw authorities off his trail, especially since the man checked into the hotel alone. Schaefer never travels without bodyguards.

Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, faces charges of sexually molesting at least five Chilean boys who attended a boarding school at Colonia Dignidad. He and other leaders of the colony, founded by Schaefer in 1961, face various other charges including illegal detention of children and obstruction of justice.
He came to Chile in the late 1950s fleeing charges of molesting boys at an orphanage he founded in Germany.

Chilean police, acting on a judge's search warrant, have made a series of inspections at the German settlement since mid-May but say they have found no obvious sign of Schaefer. Four other leaders, two of them German citizens, have been arrested recently and released on bail.
